paragraphs: We are a leading integrated energy service company, located in Midland, Texas, focused on providing innovative hydraulic fracturing, wireline, and other complementary energy and power generation services to leading upstream oil and gas companies engaged in the E&P of North American oil and natural gas resources. Our operations are primarily focused in the Permian Basin, where we have cultivated longstanding customer relationships with some of the region's most active and well‑capitalized E&P companies. The Permian Basin is widely regarded as one of the most prolific oil and natural gas producing areas in the United States, and we believe we are one of the leading providers of energy services in the region.

In December 2024, we formed a new subsidiary, ProPetro Energy Solutions, LLC, doing business as PROPWR, which provides turnkey power generation services to oil and gas producers and for general industrial projects and data centers using mobile power generation equipment installed at customers' sites. This subsidiary began revenue-generating activities during the third quarter of fiscal year 2025 and has entered into contractual arrangements with equipment manufacturers to purchase mobile natural gas-fueled power generation equipment, including turbine generator sets, reciprocating engines, auxiliary equipment and battery energy storage solution equipment.

On November 1, 2024, we sold our cementing business located in Vernal, Utah, to a business owned by a former employee as part of a strategic repositioning. We received a promissory note for $13.0 million as consideration, and recorded a gain on disposal of $8.2 million related to the sale of the business. The note receivable was fully repaid with interest in December 2025. The former employee was part of our cementing operations until November 1, 2024, and is no longer affiliated with the Company.

On May 31, 2024, we consummated the acquisition of all of the outstanding equity interests in Aqua Prop, LLC ("AquaProp"), which provides wet sand solutions for hydraulic fracturing at well sites (the "AquaProp Acquisition"). The consideration for the AquaProp Acquisition included $13.7 million of cash paid to the seller, $3.7 million of deferred cash consideration payable to the seller by May 31, 2025, the payoff of $7.2 million of the seller's outstanding debt, the payment of $0.3 million of certain transaction costs and estimated contingent consideration of $10.9 million. As a result of the AquaProp Acquisition, we expanded our business to include wet sand services.

On December 1, 2023, we consummated the purchase of the assets and operations of Par Five Energy Services LLC ("Par Five"), which provides cementing services in the Delaware Basin in exchange for $25.4 million of cash, including deferred cash consideration of $3.1 million which was payable to Par Five or its beneficiary on June 1, 2025, with interest at 4.0% per annum. (the "Par Five Acquisition"). The Par Five Acquisition complemented our existing cementing business and enabled us to serve both the Midland and Delaware sub-basins of the Permian Basin.

Collectively, the AquaProp Acquisition, the Par Five Acquisition and our acquisition of Silvertip Completion Services Operating, LLC ("Silvertip") in 2022 have positioned the Company as a more integrated and diversified completions-focused energy service provider. See "Note 4. Business Acquisitions" in the financial statements for additional disclosures.

We believe that our substantial market presence in the Permian Basin positions us well to capitalize on drilling, completion activity and power demand in the region. Our operational focus has primarily been in the Permian Basin's Midland sub-basin, where our customers have operated. However, we have increased our operations in the Delaware sub-basin and are well-positioned to support further increases in our activity in this area in response to demand from our customers. Over time, we expect the Permian Basin's Midland and Delaware sub-basins to continue to command a disproportionate share of future North American E&P spending.

Additionally, we believe the significant natural gas production in the Permian Basin will become a natural market for power-intensive businesses including data centers and other industrial businesses seeking alternative solutions for reliable and available electricity requirements which are not dependent on grid or public utility limitations.

We primarily provide hydraulic fracturing, wireline and cementing completion services to E&P companies in the Permian Basin and power generation services to oil and gas producers and non-oil and gas applications such as general industrial projects and data centers. Our completions equipment has been designed to handle the operating conditions commonly encountered in the Permian Basin and the region's increasingly high-intensity well completions (including simultaneous hydraulic fracturing

("Simul-Frac"), which involves fracturing multiple wellbores at the same time), which are characterized by longer horizontal wellbores, more stages per lateral and increasing amounts of proppant per well.

The oil and gas industry has traditionally been volatile and is characterized by a combination of long-term, short-term and cyclical trends, including domestic and international supply and demand for oil and gas, current and expected future prices for oil and gas and the perceived stability and sustainability of those prices, and capital investments of E&P companies toward their development and production of oil and gas reserves. The power generation services industry is impacted by prices and availability of electricity and power generation equipment including turbines, reciprocating engines and necessary ancillary equipment. Our power generation business will be negatively impacted if electricity prices decrease and grid power becomes widely available. The oil and gas industry and the power generation services industry are also impacted by general domestic and international economic conditions such as supply chain disruptions and inflation, war and political instability in oil producing countries, government regulations (both in the United States and internationally), levels of consumer demand, adverse weather conditions, and other factors that are beyond our control.

The geopolitical and macroeconomic consequences of military action in the Middle East, the Russian invasion of Ukraine, including the associated sanctions, recent events in Venezuela, and actions by OPEC+ have contributed to volatility in supply and demand dynamics for crude oil and associated volatility in crude oil pricing in recent years. More recently, the West Texas Intermediate ("WTI") average crude oil price declined to approximately $65 per barrel in 2025 compared to approximately $76 per barrel in 2024 in response to tariff policies implemented by the United States government, an anticipated increase in global supply of crude oil and concerns of a potential global recession resulting from high inflation, interest rates, impacts of tariff policies on supply chains and increased costs as a whole. Additionally, we have recently experienced a decrease in the Permian Basin rig count to 304 at the end of 2024 and a further decrease to 247 at the end of 2025, according to the Baker Hughes Company ("Baker Hughes"), which resulted in a reduction in the demand for completion services and pressure on pricing of our services.

Sustained levels of high inflation likewise caused the U.S. Federal Reserve and other central banks to increase interest rates, and to the extent elevated inflation remains, we may experience further cost increases for our operations, including interest rates, labor costs and equipment. We cannot predict any future trends in the rate of inflation and crude oil prices. A significant increase in or continued high levels of inflation, to the extent we are unable to timely pass-through the cost increases to our customers, further declines in crude oil prices, or potential changes in the United States' trade policy, including the imposition of tariffs and the resulting consequences, would negatively impact our business, financial condition and results of operations. See Part II, Item 1A. "Risk Factors—We may be adversely affected by the effects of inflation."

Government regulations and investors are demanding the oil and gas industry transition to a lower emissions operating environment, including upstream and energy service companies. As a result, we are working with our customers and equipment manufacturers to transition our equipment into a lower emissions profile. Currently, a number of lower emission solutions for pumping equipment, including Tier IV DGB dual-fuel, FORCE® electric, direct drive gas turbine and other technologies have been developed, and we expect additional lower emission solutions will be developed in the future. We are continually evaluating these technologies and other investment and acquisition opportunities that would support our existing and new customer relationships. The transition to lower emissions equipment is quickly evolving and will be capital intensive. Over time, we may be required to convert substantially all of our conventional Tier II equipment to lower emissions equipment. To the extent any of our customers have certain expectations or requirements with respect to emissions reductions from their contractors, if we are unable to continue quickly transitioning to lower emissions equipment, the demand for our services could be adversely impacted.

headings: Risks Inherent in Our Business and Industry
The cyclical nature of the oil and natural gas industry may cause our operating results to fluctuate.
Many of our power generation services involve long sales cycles.

Our PROPWRSM business line exposes us to the significant risks and uncertainties associated with establishment of a new line of business, and such business line may not achieve the results we anticipate.
The majority of our operations are located in the Permian Basin, making us vulnerable to risks associated with operating in one major geographic area.
Our business may be adversely affected by a deterioration in general economic conditions or a weakening of the broader energy industry.
New technology may cause us to become less competitive.
Our operations require substantial capital, and we may be unable to obtain needed capital or financing on satisfactory terms, or at all, which could limit our ability to grow.
Concerns over general economic, business or industry conditions may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, liquidity and financial condition.
Changes in U.S. trade policy and the impact of tariffs and other trade measures may have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.
Our indebtedness and liquidity needs could restrict our operations and adversely affect our financial condition.
We may record losses or impairment charges related to goodwill and long-lived assets including intangible assets.
A terrorist attack, armed conflict or political or civil unrest could harm our business.
We may be subject to claims for personal injury and property damage, which could materially adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
We are subject to cyber security risks. A cyber incident could occur and result in information theft, data corruption, operational disruptions, reputational harm and/or financial loss.
We may pursue acquisitions, internal expansions or other strategic transactions, and our failure to properly plan and manage such growth may adversely affect our performance.
We may be adversely affected by the effects of inflation.
Risks Related to Customers, Suppliers and Competition
Reliance upon a few large customers may adversely affect our revenue and operating results.
We face significant competition that may cause us to lose market share, and competition in our industry has intensified as a result of customer consolidation and industry downturns.
We expect to face significant competition in the future as the mobile and modular power industry evolves.
Our customers may not continue to outsource their power generation needs.
We are exposed to the credit risk of our customers, and any material nonpayment or nonperformance by our customers could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
We may be required to pay fees to certain of our sand suppliers based on minimum volumes under long-term contracts regardless of actual volumes received.
paragraphs: The following is a description of significant factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in forward-looking statements made in this Annual Report and presented elsewhere by management from time to time. Such factors may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. It is not possible to predict or identify all such factors. Consequently, you should not consider any such list to be a complete statement of all our potential risks or uncertainties. Due to these, and other factors, past performance should not be considered an indication of future performance.

Our business and financial performance depends on the historically cyclical oil and natural gas industry and particularly on the level of capital spending and E&P activity within the United States and in the Permian Basin, and a decline in prices for oil and natural gas may cause fluctuation in operating results or otherwise have an adverse effect on our revenue, cash flows, profitability and growth.

Demand for most of our services depends substantially on the level of capital expenditures in the Permian Basin by companies in the oil and natural gas industry Activity levels and spending by our customers and, correspondingly, demand for our services, is largely dependent on oil and natural gas prices, our customers' well completion budgets and rig count. Prolonged low oil and natural gas prices would generally depress the level of oil and natural gas exploration, development, production, and well completion activity and would result in a corresponding decline in the demand for the completion services that we provide. Historically, oil prices and markets have been extremely volatile. Prices are affected by many factors beyond our control. The average WTI oil price per barrel was approximately $65, $76 and $78 for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. In 2025, price volatility continued and crude oil prices generally declined, contributing to reductions in our customers' spending and associated drilling and completion activities, which has had and may continue to have an adverse effect on our revenue and cash flows, if the WTI oil price remains highly volatile or declines further in the future. Such trends are expected to continue in 2026. In addition, such volatility and reduction in our customers' spending and associated drilling and completion activities could also reduce the prices we receive for our services and impact the number of fleets that we are able to deploy, which would also have an adverse effect on our revenue and cash flows. See "The cyclical nature of the oil and natural gas industry may cause our operating results to fluctuate."

Many factors over which we have no control affect the supply of, and demand for our services, and our customers' willingness to explore, develop and produce oil and natural gas, and therefore, influence prices for our services, including:

•the actions by the members of OPEC+ with respect to oil production levels and announcements of potential changes in such levels, including the ability of the OPEC+ countries to agree on and comply with supply limitations;
•the domestic and foreign supply of, and demand for, oil and natural gas;

paragraphs: In January 2026, the Company sold 17.3 million shares of its common stock in an underwritten public offering for $10.00 per share, pursuant to an effective shelf registration statement on Form S-3 filed with the SEC, including shares sold pursuant to the option granted to the underwriters to purchase up to an additional 2.3 million shares of our common stock (the "2026 Common Stock Offering"). The Company received approximately $163.3 million in net proceeds from this sale after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses. The Company intends to use the net proceeds from this sale for general corporate purposes, including to fund growth capital for additional power generation equipment.

In February 2026, the Company entered into an amendment to the Caterpillar Equipment Loan Agreement, under which Caterpillar increased the availability of funds by $53.6 million, which resulted in a maximum total available amount of $157.3 million to support the purchase of certain natural gas-fueled power generation equipment.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家領先的整合型能源服務公司，位於德克薩斯州中部，專注於為從事北美油氣資源探採（E&P）的領先上游油氣公司提供創新性水力壓裂、電纜測井及其他補充性能源與發電服務。本公司業務主要集中在佩恩盆地，我們已與該地區最活躍且資金充足的E&P公司建立了長期的客戶關係。佩恩盆地被廣泛認為是美國最具生產力的油氣產區之一，我們相信本公司是該地區能源服務的主要提供者之一。
2024年12月，本公司成立了一家新子公司ProPetro Energy Solutions, LLC，以PROPWR為商號，為油氣生產者及一般工業項目與資料中心提供一站式發電服務，使用安裝於客戶現場的移動式發電設備。該子公司於財務年度2025年第三季開始產生營收，並已與設備製造商簽訂合約，購入移動式天然氣燃料發電設備，包括渦輪發電組、往復式引擎、輔助設備及電池儲能解決方案設備。
2024年11月1日，本公司將位於猶他州韋納爾的水泥注入業務出售給一位前員工所擁有之公司，作為戰略重整的一部分。本公司收到一張價值13.0百萬美元的期票作為對價，並記錄了與該業務出售相關的獲利8.2百萬美元。該應收款於2025年12月已連同利息全部償還。該前員工在2024年11月1日前為本公司水泥注入業務之一員，現已與本公司無關聯。

2024年5月31日，本公司完成購入Aqua Prop, LLC（"AquaProp"）所有已發行權益，該公司提供井場水砂解決方案用於水力壓裂（"AquaProp收購"）。AquaProp收購的對價包括支付給賣方的現金13.7百萬美元、於2025年5月31日支付給賣方的延後現金對價3.7百萬美元、償還賣方現有債務7.2百萬美元、支付交易費用0.3百萬美元及預估的或有對價10.9百萬美元。因AquaProp收購，本公司業務已擴展至包含水砂服務。

2023年12月1日，本公司完成購入Par Five Energy Services LLC（"Par Five"）的資產與業務，該公司提供水泥注入服務於德克薩斯州德克薩斯盆地，對價為現金25.4百萬美元，包括於2025年6月1日支付給Par Five或其受益人的延後現金對價3.1百萬美元，年利率為4.0%。（"Par Five收購"）。Par Five收購補強了本公司現有水泥注入業務，使本公司能同時服務佩恩盆地的米德蘭與德克薩斯子盆地。
整體而言，AquaProp收購、Par Five收購以及本公司於2022年收購Silvertip Completion Services Operating, LLC（"Silvertip"）使本公司成為更具整合性與多元化的完井專注能源服務提供者。有關更多披露資訊，請參閱財務報表中的"附註4. 企業併購"。
本公司相信在佩恩盆地的廣泛市場佔有率，使本公司能有效把握該地區鑽井、完井活動與發電需求。本公司業務主要集中在佩恩盆地的米德蘭子盆地，而客戶的運營亦於此進行。然而，本公司已增加在德克薩斯子盆地的業務，並具備良好的條件以支持該地區因客戶需求而進一步增加活動量。長期而言，本公司預期佩恩盆地的米德蘭與德克薩斯子盆地將持續佔據未來北美E&P支出的不成比例份額。
此外，本公司相信佩恩盆地的大量天然氣生產將成為對電力需求高的企業，包括資料中心及其他工業企業尋求可靠且可用電力解決方案的自然市場，這些解決方案不依賴於電網或公共電力供應的限制。
我們主要為 Permian Basin 的 E&P 公司提供水力壓裂、電纜線及水泥完井服務，並為油氣生產商及非油氣應用領域（例如一般工業專案及資料中心）提供發電服務。我們的完井設備已設計用以處理 Permian Basin 及該地區日益強烈的井完井作業（包括同時進行水力壓裂
"Simul-Frac"), 哪涉及同時對多口井進行壓裂作業), 這些作業特徵為較長的水平井, 每個側向分段數量更多, 以及每口井使用的壓裂砂量增加。

油氣產業傳統上具有波動性, 並特徵為長期、短期及週期性趨勢的組合, 包括國內外油氣的供給與需求, 當前及預期未來的油氣價格, 以及對這些價格的穩定性與可持續性之看法, 以及探採公司對其油氣儲量開發與生產的資本投資。電力發電服務產業受電力與發電設備(包括渦輪機、往復式引擎及必要輔助設備)的價格與可得性影響。若電力價格下降且電網電力廣泛可用, 我們的電力發電業務將受到負面影響。油氣產業與電力發電服務產業亦受總體經濟條件影響, 如供應鏈中斷與通貨膨脹, 油氣生產國的戰爭與政治不穩定, 政府規範(美國與國際皆然), 消費者需求水平, 不利天氣條件, 以及其他超出我們控制範疇的因素。

中東地區軍事行動的國際政治與總體經濟後果、俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭包括相關制裁、委內瑞拉近期事件，以及 OPEC+ 的行動，已導致近期原油供應與需求動態的波動，以及原油價格的波動。更近期，西德克薩斯中間基準（"WTI"）原油平均價格在 2025 年下跌至每桶約 65 美元，與 2024 年每桶約 76 美元相比，這是因應美國政府實施的關稅政策、預期全球原油供應增加，以及因高通貨膨脹、利率、關稅政策對供應鏈的影響及整體成本上升而產生的潛在全球經濟衰退擔憂所致。此外，我們近期觀察到 Permian Basin 的鑽井數量下降至 2024 年年底的 304 口，並進一步下降至 2025 年年底的 247 口，根據 Baker Hughes 公司（"Baker Hughes"）的資料，這導致完成服務需求減少，並對我們服務的價格造成壓力。

持續的高通貨膨脹也促使美國聯邦儲備理事會及其他中央銀行提高利率，若通貨膨脹持續高企，我們可能面臨進一步的運營成本增加，包括利率、人工成本及設備成本。我們無法預測未來通貨膨脹率及原油價格的趨勢。若通貨膨脹率大幅上升或持續高企，且我們無法及時將成本增加轉嫁給客戶，原油價格進一步下跌，或美國貿易政策出現變動，包括關稅的實施及其後果，將對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。請參閱第二部分，第 1A 項 "風險因素—我們可能因通貨膨脹的影響而受到不利影響。"

政府規範與投資者要求油氣產業轉型為低排放運作環境，包括上游及能源服務公司。因此，我們正與客戶及設備製造商合作，將我們的設備轉型為低排放型態。目前，已開發出多種低排放解決方案，包括 Tier IV DGB 雙燃料、FORCE® 電動、直接驅動氣渦輪機及其他技術，我們預期未來將有更多低排放解決方案問世。我們持續評估這些技術及其他投資與收購機會，以支持我們現有及新客戶的關係。轉型為低排放設備的過程迅速演進，且將需要大量資金投入。長遠而言，我們可能需要將大部分傳統 Tier II 設備轉型為低排放設備。若任何客戶對承包商的減排有特定期待或要求，而我們無法持續快速轉型為低排放設備，則我們的服務需求可能受到不利影響。

paragraphs: 民國115年1月，本公司於公開發行的承銷股票發行中出售17.3百萬股普通股，每股價格為10.00美元，依據向SEC提交的Form S-3有效shelf registration statement進行，包含根據承銷商獲授權可購買最多2.3百萬股本公司普通股的選擇權（"2026普通股發行"）。本公司在扣除承銷折扣與佣金及預估發行費用後，自此次發行中獲得約163.3百萬美元的淨資金。本公司預計將此次發行的淨資金用於一般企業用途，包括用以資助新增的發電設備之成長性資本。
2026 年 2 月，本公司與 Caterpillar 簽訂了 Caterpillar 裝置貸款協議的修正案，根據該修正案，Caterpillar 將資金可運用額增加 53.6 百萬美元，使得資金總可運用額達到 157.3 百萬美元，用以支持購買特定天然氣燃料發電設備。

headings: 業務與產業內固有的風險
油氣產業的週期性可能導致我們的營運成果產生波動。
我們許多的電力發電服務涉及長銷售週期。
我們的 PROPWRSM 事業線使我們面臨建立新事業線所伴隨的重大風險與不確定性，且該事業線可能無法達成我們預期的結果。
我們的業務主要位於 Permian Basin，使我們面臨在單一主要地理區域營運的風險。
總體經濟條件惡化或能源產業整體趨勢走弱可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
新技術可能使我們變得較不具競爭力。
我們的營運需要大量資金，我們可能無法以滿意的條件或完全無法取得所需資金或融資，這可能會限制我們的成長能力。
對總體經濟、商業或產業條件的擔憂，可能對本公司的營運成果、流動性及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
美國貿易政策的變動及關稅及其他貿易措施的影響，可能對本公司業務及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司的負債及流動性需求，可能限制本公司營運，並對財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司可能因商譽及長期資產（包括無形資產）而記錄虧損或減損費用。
恐怖攻擊、武裝衝突或政治或內亂，可能損害本公司業務。
本公司可能面臨個人傷害及財產損壞的索賠，這可能對財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司面臨網路安全風險。網路事件可能發生，導致資訊竊取、資料毀損、營運中斷、聲譽損害及/或財務損失。
本公司可能進行收購、內部擴張或其他戰略交易，若未能妥善規劃及管理此類成長，可能對表現造成不利影響。
我們可能因通貨膨脹的影響而遭受不利影響。
與客戶、供應商及競爭對手相關的風險
對少數大型客戶的依賴可能對我們的營業收入及營運成果造成不利影響。
我們面臨著顯著的競爭，可能導致我們失去市佔率，且因客戶集中及產業景氣衰退，產業競爭已顯著加劇。
我們預期未來在行動及模組化電力產業發展的過程中，將面臨顯著的競爭。
我們的客戶可能不會持續委外其電力產生需求。
我們面臨客戶信用風險，若客戶有重大未付款或未履行契約的情況，可能對我們的業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
我們可能因與砂石供應商簽訂的長期契約中約定的最低採購量，而需支付相關費用，與實際採購量無關。
paragraphs: 下列為可能導致實際結果與本年度報告中所作之預測性陳述及管理階層不時於其他地方所作之預測性陳述有重大差異的重要因素。這些因素可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。無法預測或識別所有這些因素。因此，您不應將任何此類清單視為本公司所有潛在風險或不確定性的完整陳述。由於這些及其他因素，過去表現不應視為未來表現的指標。
本公司業務及財務表現取決於歷史性週期性的油氣產業，特別是美國及帕默勒盆地內的資本支出及探採活動水準，油氣價格下跌可能導致營運結果波動，或對本公司營收、現金流、獲利能力及成長產生不利影響。

我們大多數服務的需求基本上取決於帕默勒盆地內油氣產業公司之資本支出水準，客戶的活動水準及支出，以及相應的我們服務需求，主要取決於油氣價格、客戶的井完井預算及鑽井數量。長期低油氣價格將通常壓抑油氣探採、開發、生產及井完井活動，並導致我們所提供的完井服務需求相應減少。歷來，油價及市場極為波動。價格受許多超出本公司控制範疇的因素影響。截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日止，平均WTI原油價格每桶約為65美元、76美元及78美元。在2025年，價格波動持續，原油價格普遍下跌，導致客戶支出減少及相關鑽井與完井活動減少，這已對本公司營收及現金流產生不利影響，並可能持續產生不利影響，如果WTI原油價格持續高度波動或進一步下跌。此種趨勢預期將在2026年持續。此外，這種波動及客戶支出減少及相關鑽井與完井活動減少，也可能降低我們所收取服務價格，並影響我們能夠部署的 fleets 數量，這也會對本公司營收及現金流產生不利影響。請參閱『油氣產業的週期性特質可能導致本公司營運結果波動。』
許多我們無法控制的因素影響我們服務的供給與需求，以及客戶對探採及生產油氣的意願，因此影響我們服務的價格，包括：
•OPEC+成員國關於石油產量水準的行動及對可能變動該水準的公告，包括OPEC+國家同意並遵守產量限制的能力；
•國內及國際油氣的供給與需求
